Analysis — fleet configuration analytics

A product-specific analytics page per ADOM, built from SATOM's cache — inventory, server policies, protection profiles, backends, exceptions, App IDs, segments and change activity on FortiWeb; delivery, security and TLS posture on FortiADC; entitlement and identity on FortiAuthenticator; log rate and storage on FortiAnalyzer.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view users.manage operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereMonitoring → Analysis (every ADOM) (URL /analysis/)

What is it?#

Analysis turns the configuration SATOM has harvested into charts and findings. It is different in every ADOM, because a WAF, a load balancer, an identity server and a log collector fail in different ways. Except for the live FortiAnalyzer panels, the page reads only the local cache (and, for FortiAuthenticator, the metrics store), so it never contacts an appliance.

What does it do?#

ADOM Page title Content
FortiWeb and Global Analysis Devices (by platform, zone, line, department, status); object inventory per section and type; server policies (deployment mode, status, traffic log, TLS exposure, per device, full list); web protection profiles (kind, per device, usage, which WPP per device, unused WPP); backends & services (pools by type/protocol/device, HTTP ports, HTTPS service); exceptions (category, type, device, duplicates); application IDs (coverage, list, policies without an App ID); network segments (IPs per segment); change activity (timeline, by action, by device, audit by action, recent changes); Deep Analysis (fleet inventory, back-end ports, per-device inventory, WPP feature coverage, sub-elements captured, unused WPP orphans, drill-down explorer), FortiADC depth capture included
FortiADC Analysis — delivery Findings; virtual servers (type, admin status, reported availability, list); pools, members and real servers with health-check coverage; security defined versus applied (WAF and IPS profiles); TLS posture (client-SSL profiles allowing legacy TLS, local certificates with days left); object inventory (child tables from the depth capture included); cache freshness
FortiAuthenticator Analysis — identity Entitlement (licence headroom from the metrics store); authentication posture findings; identity inventory; cache freshness
FortiAnalyzer Analysis (FortiAnalyzer) Live: incoming log rate by device and storage & quota by ADOM (analytics and archive used/quota, retention days); devices; object inventory; change activity

An ADOM without a page of its own shows No analysis page is built for this ADOM yet. instead of another product's dashboard.

Requirements#

  • Harvested configuration of the devices (device_sync / rediscovery).
  • For Deep Analysis on FortiWeb: a deep capture (the full WPP sub-tree and policy dependency graph), started with Run deep capture.
  • For FortiADC objects in Deep Analysis and the FortiADC child-table counts: a rediscovery of the FortiADC with Capture full depth: every child table (REST) on. Run deep capture does not read FortiADC child tables.
  • For the FortiAuthenticator entitlement section: the capacity collector (see Metrics collection).
  • For FortiAnalyzer live panels: the analyser reachable over its API.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Viewing: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view; all system profiles have it. A custom profile with no read key gets 403.
  • Run deep capture: the legacy config_write gate (e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply).
  • Save pattern (App ID pattern): users.manage (Administrator).
  • Each control is shown only to users who hold its permission: Run deep capture to config_write holders, the App ID pattern form with Save pattern to administrators. A direct request without the right answers 403.
  • Deep reads, drill-downs and deep captures cover only the devices you can see in the current ADOM (maintenance devices stay hidden unless you hold appliances.view_maintenance).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Analysis now needs a read permission instead of sign-in alone, its deep panels, drill-downs and Run deep capture are limited to the devices visible to you, and Save pattern / Run deep capture are shown only to users who may use them.

How to use#

Filter the FortiWeb/Global page#

  1. Choose Platform, Zone, Line, Department and/or Devices (ctrl=multi); for change activity, Changes from / Changes to.
  2. Click Apply (Reset clears). Refresh reloads the data.
  3. Click ⤢ on a chart to expand it, change chart type, top-N, and export CSV/PNG.

Set the App ID pattern (administrators)#

Enter a regular expression in App ID pattern (regex, from Server Policy comment) (default app\d{5}, case-insensitive) and click Save pattern. The App ID section then extracts IDs from server policy comments with it.

Run a deep capture#

In Deep Analysis — WPP & Policy Depth, click Run deep capture. With no device filter, every FortiWeb visible to you in the ADOM is captured; devices you pick outside that set are ignored. The job runs in the background (up to 8 devices in parallel) and is resumable. Reload refreshes the deep panels; the freshness chips show how old each device's deep data is.

Drill down#

In Drill-down explorer, choose the type — Web Protection Profile, Server Policy or FortiADC object (child tables) — and pick an object to see its full captured sub-tree or dependency graph. The FortiADC type lists every captured parent object of the FortiADC devices (pools, certificate groups, content routing, schedule groups…) as device · type · name, and opens it with its child-table members.

FortiADC in the deep panels#

The FortiADC depth capture is part of the deep layer, so the Deep Analysis panels count it beside the FortiWeb data:

  • Sub-elements captured includes the FortiADC child tables (stored as <parent>/<child>, for example load_balance_pool/pool_member).
  • Fleet inventory counts FortiADC pools in Server pools (shown as N FortiADC beside the unique / shared FortiWeb pools) and FortiADC pool members as back-ends, with their IPs and ports, in the back-end ports chart and the Per-device inventory.

On the FortiADC ADOM's Analysis — delivery page, the object inventory counts the 27 <parent>_child_<table> tables from the depth capture. Without a depth capture they read 0, because the sweep never reads child tables.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Platform / Zone / Line / Department Device facets No DMZ
Devices (ctrl=multi) Restrict to devices No fweb-01, fweb-02
Changes from / to Date window for change activity No 2026-09-01
App ID pattern Regex applied to server-policy comments No app\d{5}

Example#

🧪Example — Find protection profiles nobody uses

Open Analysis in the FortiWeb ADOM, run a deep capture once, and read Unused WPP (orphans): every web protection profile no server policy binds.

Result#

  • Run deep capture starts a background job and writes audit entry analysis.deep_run; the deep cache is updated per device.
  • Save pattern writes analysis.appid_regex and flashes App ID pattern saved: <pattern>.

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid regular expression: …"#

The App ID pattern does not compile. Fix the regex.

"No FortiADC appliance is visible in this ADOM." / "No FortiAuthenticator appliance is visible in this ADOM."#

Register a device of that product or switch ADOM.

FortiADC findings say "not harvested"#

A section that was never harvested produces a finding rather than a reassuring zero — run a rediscovery of the device.

FortiAnalyzer panels: "No FortiAnalyzer appliance in scope" or "<device>: login …"#

No analyser is visible, or the login to it failed. Check the device credentials.

Deep panels are empty#

No deep capture has run. Click Run deep capture (needs config_write), or ask a user with that right.

No FortiADC objects in the drill-down, or FortiADC child tables read 0#

The FortiADC object (child tables) list says (none captured) until a FortiADC has been rediscovered with Capture full depth: every child table (REST) on. A depth capture taken before SATOM filed it in the deep layer is not counted either. Run that rediscovery again; see Discovery and rediscovery.

"Run deep capture" or "Save pattern" is missing#

The button is shown only with the permission named in Permissions: config_write for Run deep capture, users.manage for Save pattern.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • FortiAuthenticator percentages are only shown where the device reports a ceiling; a counter without one is shown as no ceiling — no percentage.
  • FortiADC certificate expiry is read at day precision.
  • The deep-analysis JSON endpoints (/analysis/wpp-matrix, /subelements, /orphans, /deep/*) intersect the device filter you pass with the devices you can see; with no filter they cover every visible device. A drill-down (/analysis/deep/wpp/<id>/…, /deep/policy/<id>/…, /deep/object/<id>/<type>/…) for a device you cannot see answers 404.
  • /analysis/dashboard/<id> redirects to this page filtered to one device (used by links from the appliance page).
